evals.name: company-memberships-alone-vs-combined
evals.prompt: I'm prepping a briefing for IBM's leadership. How many Linux Foundation memberships does IBM hold today and what are they worth? I need two views: IBM on its own, and IBM as a group including Red Hat and any other subsidiaries. Use the LFX MCP tools.
evals.expected_output: Resolves the legal account name before querying; reports the memberships family as project-account pairs with list-price value, side by side and never divided; two readings (account alone, subsidiaries combined) named as a scope choice; says 'as of today'; does not count membership records into the figure; a zero for the everyday name 'IBM' is treated as a wrong name, not an answer; provenance block with lane, scope, window, population.
assertions: Resolves IBM to the stored legal account name (International Business Machines Corporation) before any membership figure is quoted; the everyday name 'IBM' is not the scope of a reported figure
Reports the membership count and the list-price value side by side and never divides one by the other or calls the value 'dues billed'
Gives two readings named as a scope choice: the IBM account alone and IBM including subsidiaries (combined), each from its own standard-metrics call
States the reading is as of today (or the run date) and describes the count as memberships/project-account pairs, not as 'member organisations'
Does not count membership records from search_members into the headline figure (record tools may be used for context only)
Carries a provenance block or equivalent with scope as applied, window/as-of date and the population/definition
The per-subsidiary breakdown (separate) reconciles to the combined total, and every figure in the answer appears in the call log
No provenance claim is made that the call log does not support (for example, 'compiled SQL kept with the working files' when no SQL was kept)

evals.name: foundation-participants-vs-contributors-top-companies
evals.prompt: For CNCF and all its projects: how many developers took part over the last 12 months, and how does that compare with people who actually contributed code? Then give me the top 5 companies by volume of code contributions in that period. Use the LFX MCP tools.
evals.expected_output: Resolves cncf via search_projects; uses the participants family (any non-bot activity) as the answer to 'took part' and the contributors family as the narrower reading; uses the contributions family by organisation for the ranking; the unattributed (NULL) row is reported as unattributed and dropped from the ranking, which is re-sorted; window stated as concrete dates; bots excluded stated once; foundation scope 'CNCF and its projects', never the umbrella slug.
assertions: Resolves the CNCF slug via search_projects before the data calls and scopes the figures to CNCF and its projects (not the umbrella foundation slug, not LF-wide)

Answers 'took part' with the participants family (any non-bot activity: code, issues, reviews, comments, stars, forks, meetings, training, Hacker News) and presents code contributors as the narrower reading, with both figures stated
Uses the contributions family grouped by organisation for the top-5 ranking, with the unattributed/NULL row excluded from the ranking and mentioned as unattributed
States the window as concrete dates (start and end) and says bots are excluded
Does not sum per-organisation or per-project rows to produce a headcount total

The first organisation ranking call requests more rows than the top-N asked for, so the unattributed row does not cost a re-run; and every comparative aside in the answer matches the rows in the call log

evals.name: board-seats-and-meeting-count-service-tools
evals.prompt: Who represents Google on the CNCF Governing Board right now (name, role, voting status), and how many CNCF Technical Oversight Committee meetings have taken place in 2026 so far? Use the LFX MCP tools.
evals.expected_output: Finds the CNCF project uid, finds the Governing Board committee by project and name, paginates the roster to the end and filters by organisation client-side; names people only in the roster context; finds the TOC committee and counts past meetings by project and date range, filtered to that committee, paginated; labels both as 'visible to you'; does not infer seats from tier or activity; does not use the semantic layer or lens for either.
assertions: Finds the CNCF Governing Board through the committee tools (search_committees scoped to the CNCF project) and lists Google's representatives with name, role and voting status from search_committee_members
Paginates the roster (follows page tokens until none) or explicitly states the roster was read to the end before filtering by organisation
Counts TOC meetings in 2026 from the past-meetings tool scoped to the project and date range (and the TOC committee), not from the semantic layer or lens
Labels the roster and the meeting count as what is visible to the caller ('visible to you' or equivalent), not as an LF total
Does not infer any seat from membership tier, sponsorship or activity data
Both Technical Oversight Committee records (Public and Private) are checked before the meeting count is given, and no unscoped committee search across all foundations is made

evals.name: new-members-per-year-and-org-reading
evals.prompt: How many new members joined the Linux Foundation per year over the last five years? And separately, can you tell me how many organisations were brand new to the LF each year, as opposed to existing members joining another project? Use the LFX MCP tools.
evals.expected_output: Uses the new_members family as a bare series by year without a hand-computed start date, quotes each year from its own row, marks the current year to-date, and names the grain (one per project, organisation and install day). For 'brand new to the LF' uses the new-member-organisations family LF-wide as a governed series of distinct organisations, states the level of arrival the result gives (a lapsed organisation that returns counts as new again), offers the first-ever reading as the layer's first-membership dimension and says it counts memberships rather than organisations, bounds the current year at today, and presents the two series as different grains, never one derived from the other.
assertions: Uses the new_members family as a series by year without a hand-computed start date (bare period series or the family default), LF-wide with no project set
Quotes each year from its own row, marks the current year as year-to-date/partial and says which years the table shows
Explains the grain of new memberships: one per project, organisation and install day, so an organisation joining another project counts again and a returning pair counts again on its new install day

For the 'brand new to the LF' question, uses the new-member-organisations family (organisations arriving in the year: no membership anywhere in the LF the day before), LF-wide, as a governed figure, and says a lapsed account that rejoins counts as new again while a first-ever reading is the layer's first-membership dimension

States the level of arrival the applied block gives (the LF, since no project was named), heads the column as organisations, and presents the two series (new memberships vs new organisations) as different grains, never one derived from the other

The current year is bounded at today (installs can be future-dated) and the new-organisations figure sits at or below the new-memberships figure for the same year, with the reason stated (an organisation joining two programmes counts once here, twice there)
Carries a provenance block or equivalent with scope, window and population
Offers the first-ever reading as an alternative (the layer's first-membership dimension), says it counts membership rows rather than organisations, and does not head it 'new organisations'

While the standard-metric lag stands, the answer quotes the family's rows as arrivals and does not repeat the family's lagging definition sentence ('first membership') as the reading; the provenance says which path ran

evals.name: umbrella-slug-memberships-by-country-no-subtree
evals.prompt: Two quick questions for a board pre-read. First, is CNCF part of The Linux Foundation's project tree, and where does Kubernetes sit in it? Second, how many countries have organisations with an active membership in The Linux Foundation itself (as opposed to its sub-foundations), and which are the top five countries by number of memberships? Use the LFX MCP tools.
evals.expected_output: Resolves the umbrella's own slug via search_projects and explains that on memberships that slug is one membership programme (the LF's own), not a subtree; sibling or hosted foundations' memberships carry their own slugs and are neither included nor 'excluded'; no child-project count is attached to the figure; the unresolved-country row is reported as unresolved and not counted as a country; the reading is pairs, as of today; the top five come from the by-country breakdown re-sorted with the NULL row dropped.
assertions: Answers the tree question from the project tools (search_projects / get_project): CNCF is a child of the umbrella foundation and Kubernetes sits under CNCF; never says CNCF is not part of the LF, and never answers the tree from memory

Uses a membership family grouped by country — the member-organisations family (distinct organisations) or the memberships family (project-account pairs) — scoped to the umbrella's own slug (resolved via search_projects) and says in plain words that the scope is the LF's own membership programme, one slug, not a subtree of projects

Never narrates the scope as 'projects directly hosted under the LF', never attaches a child-project count from search_projects to the membership figure, and never says other foundations were 'excluded' from a tree
Reports the NULL / unresolved country row as unresolved (accounts whose country is not known or whose stored spelling the lens does not resolve) and does not count it as a country
States the reading is as of today and names the grain it reports (organisations or project-account pairs), and gives the top five countries from the breakdown with the NULL row dropped before ranking
Carries a provenance block with scope as applied, as-of date and the population sentence

States explicitly that the project tree and the membership programme are different axes, so that 'CNCF is a child of the LF' and 'CNCF memberships are not in the LF's own programme' are both true and neither contradicts the other

evals.name: axis2-activity-scope-tree-vs-bucket
evals.prompt: How many people contributed code to CNCF over the last 12 months, and how many of those were on Kubernetes specifically? Also: does the CNCF figure include Kubernetes and the other CNCF projects, or is it CNCF on its own? Use the LFX MCP tools.
evals.expected_output: Contributors for cncf (default = whole tree, folded) and for k8s; explains that the default reading is CNCF and everything beneath it on the project spine, that Kubernetes is inside it, and that a distinct count for the tree is not the sum of project rows; the CNCF-alone bucket is a different reading it names as such.
assertions: States that the CNCF contributors figure covers CNCF and all its projects at any depth (the default folded reading), not CNCF's own bucket alone, and that Kubernetes' contributors are inside it
Does not present the CNCF figure as 'CNCF itself, excluding its projects', and does not sum project rows into a tree headcount
Both figures come from the contributors family with the window stated as dates and bots excluded, and the two slugs come from search_projects
Carries a provenance block with scope as applied (tree vs bucket named), window and population

evals.name: axis3-switches-separate-vs-combined
evals.prompt: Break down Amazon's code contributions to Linux Foundation projects over the last 12 months by subsidiary (AWS and the rest), and tell me the total for Amazon as a group. Use the LFX MCP tools.
evals.expected_output: Resolves the legal name; the group total is the combined reading in its own call; the breakdown is the separate reading by organisation; the answer says the account-alone default was not what ran; contributions are additive so the rows reconcile to the combined figure, and the answer still takes the total from the combined call rather than summing rows.
assertions: The group total comes from a combined reading (its own call), and the per-subsidiary rows from a separate reading; the total is not produced by adding the separate rows
The answer names the scope choice: the account alone is the default and was not what was reported; the group figure is Amazon including its subsidiaries at any depth
The legal account name is resolved before querying, and the breakdown reconciles to the combined total (stated as a check, since contributions are additive)
Window stated as dates, bots excluded, provenance block present

evals.name: axis4-org-vocabularies-never-mixed
evals.prompt: Compare Red Hat's Linux Foundation memberships with the number of organisations credited with code contributions to OpenShift-related LF projects — actually, simpler: how many memberships does Red Hat hold, and how many distinct organisations contributed code to CNCF in the last 12 months? Is Red Hat one of them? Use the LFX MCP tools.
evals.expected_output: Memberships for the Red Hat LLC account (CRM legal name); contributing organisations for cncf from the contributing-organisations family, which uses the enrichment vocabulary; says the two vocabularies differ and that 'Red Hat' in the enrichment data and 'Red Hat LLC' in the CRM are not the same row; answers whether Red Hat appears in the contributing organisations via the enrichment spelling, without mixing the counts.
assertions: Memberships are scoped to the stored legal name (Red Hat LLC) resolved this session, and its parent (International Business Machines Corporation) is mentioned as the parent, not folded in

The contributing-organisations figure is taken from that family (or the equivalent) and described as organisations as the contribution data names them, a different vocabulary from the CRM account names
The answer says explicitly that the two vocabularies are not mixed and does not present 'Red Hat' (enrichment) and 'Red Hat LLC' (account) as one row or compare the two counts as like for like
Provenance block present for each figure with scope, window and population

evals.name: axis5-time-windows-vs-as-of
evals.prompt: How many memberships did the LF have at the end of 2024, how many new memberships were sold in 2025, and how many does it have right now? Use the LFX MCP tools.
evals.expected_output: Three readings: an as-of reading on 2024-12-31 (date-based, said so), a window reading for calendar 2025 as dates, and today's status-based reading; the answer never applies the trailing-twelve-months default to the 2025 question, never calls the year-end figure 'today', and states each window or date in words.
assertions: The end-of-2024 figure is an as-of reading on 2024-12-31 from the memberships family and is described as date-based as of that date, not as 'today'
The 2025 new-memberships figure is a window reading with the calendar year as concrete dates (not the trailing-twelve-months default) and is described as new project memberships by install date
Today's figure is the status-based current reading and is described as of today; the answer explains that the as-of and today readings are two kinds
No window is computed by hand into a series and no partial period is quoted as full; provenance block present

evals.name: axis6-population-registrations-vs-people
evals.prompt: For LF events in the last 12 months: how many registrations were there, how many different people registered, and how many actually showed up? And how many people took part in LF projects overall in that period — not just coders? Use the LFX MCP tools.
evals.expected_output: Registrations family: records, distinct registrants by e-mail, checked-in attendees only where the source carries check-in (a zero can mean no check-in data); participants family for 'took part'; each population sentence from the applied block in the reader's words; distinct counts never summed.
assertions: Registrations, distinct registrants and checked-in attendees are presented as three populations from the registrations family, with the caveat that check-in exists only for some registration sources (zero attendees is not zero attendance)

'Took part, not just coders' is answered with the participants family (any non-bot activity: code, issues, reviews, comments, stars, forks, meetings, training, Hacker News) and described in those words, with contributors named as the narrower alternative
The window is stated as dates and described as by event start date for the events figures
No population is renamed (no 'attendees' for registrations, no 'developers' for contributors without qualification); provenance block present

evals.name: axis7-geography-whose-country
evals.prompt: How many countries do LF member organisations come from, and how many countries do our code contributors come from? Which is the bigger footprint? Use the LFX MCP tools.
evals.expected_output: Memberships by country: the account's billing country, conformed, with an unresolved row that is not a country; contributors by country: the person's country, known for a minority, with a NULL row; the answer says the two follow different subjects (account vs person), does not count the unresolved rows as countries, and says the region grouping is provisional if regions are mentioned.
assertions: The membership country count is described as the billing country of the member account (conformed), and the unresolved/NULL row is excluded from the count and reported as unresolved
The contributor country count is described as the person's own country, known for a minority of contributors, with the NULL row excluded from the count and reported
The answer states that the two figures follow different subjects (account vs person) and does not present them as the same kind of footprint without that caveat
Provenance block present; any region mention carries the provisional note

evals.name: axis8-ranking-limits-identities
evals.prompt: Who are the top ten contributors to the Linux kernel over the last 12 months, and which organisations are the top five? Use the LFX MCP tools.
evals.expected_output: Contributions by contributor for the kernel slug (identities by handle, display names can be shared) presented only as appropriate; contributions by organisation with the unattributed row dropped and the ranking re-sorted; the answer says the lists are the top N shown, never 'all', and names the unattributed share once.
assertions: The kernel slug is resolved via search_projects and both rankings come from the contributions family with the window stated as dates and bots excluded
The organisation ranking excludes the unattributed/NULL row (re-sorted before the top five is read) and the unattributed share is stated once
The people ranking is described as by identity (handle), presented in a way appropriate to naming individuals, and two identities are not merged into one person
The answer says 'the top N shown' rather than 'all', and provenance block present

evals.name: axis9-lens-scope-line
evals.prompt: Using the SQL assistant: how many distinct accepted speakers were there at events belonging to CNCF in the last 12 months, and how many across all LF events? Use the LFX MCP tools.
evals.expected_output: Two lens questions with concrete dates: one with the cncf slug in the scope list, one with no scope (LF-wide, said so); each answer opens with the scope line the tool returned; the CNCF figure is not narrated as 'CNCF and its projects' unless the scope line shows those slugs; both labelled generated SQL and cross-framed against the speakers family where it applies.
assertions: The requested lane is honoured: the SQL assistant is run (its figures labelled generated SQL, each answer repeating the scope line the tool returned) — and when the speakers family is used as the answer, the assistant's reading is still shown beside it, never silently replaced
The CNCF reading is not narrated as covering CNCF's projects beyond what the scope line shows, and the LF-wide reading is described as no project filter, not as the umbrella's slug
Concrete dates are written into the assistant's question, the speakers population is accepted speakers, distinct people, and the LF-wide figure is cross-framed against the speakers family
Provenance block present with the SQL kept only if it was kept

evals.name: lf-wide-meetings-held-hours-people-ad-hoc
evals.prompt: How many meetings were held across all Linux Foundation projects in the last twelve months, how many hours of meetings was that, and how many different people attended? Use the LFX MCP tools.
evals.expected_output: Meeting occurrences, scheduled minutes and unique attendees from the semantic layer's named meeting metrics, LF-wide with no project set, the window bounded at today; hours said to be scheduled rather than time spent; people said to be distinct users (e-mail as the fallback), below attendances; every meeting figure a floor by platform onboarding; labelled ad hoc, cited as all meetings in the warehouse, not 'visible to you'.
assertions: Reads meeting occurrences, scheduled minutes and unique attendees through the semantic layer (explore then query), LF-wide with no project set, and does not use the count tool or the SQL assistant for the LF-wide totals
Labels the three figures ad hoc (a semantic-layer reading), not governed, interim or generated SQL, and cites them as all meetings in the warehouse rather than as visible to the caller
Says hours are scheduled duration summed once per occurrence, not time spent and not person-hours
Says people are distinct attendees identified by LF user or e-mail, distinct from attendances, and never counts invitee ids
States the window as concrete dates bounded at today and calls every meeting figure a floor bounded by platform onboarding

evals.name: social-reach-impressions-not-audience
evals.prompt: What is the Linux Foundation's social media reach since tracking began, and how many mentions and authors is that based on? Use the LFX MCP tools.
evals.expected_output: Social-reach and social-mentions families LF-wide over the all-history default; reach worded as potential impressions, follower counts summed per mention, never audience or people reached; the one-network limitation stated; the start of the feed read from a monthly series or the coverage sentence, not a yearly bucket; not added across projects.
assertions: Uses the social-reach and social-mentions families LF-wide with no project set and without a hand-computed start date
Words reach as potential impressions or an equivalent that says follower counts are summed per mention, and never as audience, people reached or unique followers
States that follower counts exist for one network only, so reach covers that network
States the start of the feed from a monthly series or the family's coverage sentence, never inferred from a yearly bucket
Carries a provenance block with scope, window and population

evals.name: lost-organisations-departures-on-the-day
evals.prompt: How many organisations did the Linux Foundation lose each year over the last four years, and does that include companies that later came back? Use the LFX MCP tools.
evals.expected_output: Lost organisations as departures: a paid term that ended with no other term of the organisation covering the next day, judged on that day, so a later return does not undo it and free-term lapses are not departures. While the lens lag stands, departures judged on the day come from the semantic layer's lost-organisations metric, labelled ad hoc, because the standard-metric family still excludes organisations that have since returned; if the family is quoted at all it is labelled as excluding returners and is not called departures. The current year bounded at today; the churn date is the day after the term ends.
assertions: Defines a lost organisation as a paid departure judged on the day it happened (no other term covering the next day), says a later return does not undo it, and says a free or zero-price lapse is not a departure

While the lens lag stands, takes departures judged on the day from the semantic layer's lost-organisations metric (labelled ad hoc) rather than the standard-metric family; if the family's figure is quoted at all, it is labelled as excluding organisations that have since returned and is not presented as departures; the provenance says which path ran
Bounds the current year at today and says the churn date is the day after the term ends, so a year-end lapse lands in the next year
Does not derive lost organisations from churned memberships (a company that dropped one project and kept another churned but is not lost)
Carries a provenance block with scope, window and population
